# Summary of Information on Philip Rubin
Philip Rubin is a cognitive scientist whose work integrates computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological approaches, focusing primarily on the biological bases of speech and language. He is notably recognized for his contributions to articulatory synthesis, speech perception, sinewave synthesis, signal processing, and modeling complex temporal events. Rubin developed key computational tools at Haskins Laboratories, including ASY (an articulatory synthesis program) and SWS (a sinewave synthesis program), and advanced theoretical models such as CASY and TADA for speech production and coordination. His research emphasized embodied cognition, event-based modeling, multimodal speech processing, and perceptual organization, and he collaborated with many colleagues to refine gestural and dynamical systems perspectives on speech.
In addition to his scientific research, Rubin has held significant leadership roles in science administration, policy, and advocacy. He served as Director of the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the National Science Foundation (NSF), was Assistant Director for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), and has been involved in ethical oversight of human subject research. Rubin has been active in various advisory committees, scholarly boards, and advocacy groups, and currently serves as President of the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences. His career includes extensive contributions to advancing interdisciplinary research, science policy, and ethical considerations in emerging technologies.
